q: 1. The zone in which transverse bending is likely to occur may be obtained by drawing a line from the faces to the column making an angle 'θ' with the horizontal where 'θ' may be ...........
explain: A 45-degree dispersion is commonly assumed for the distribution of loads and stresses in thick concrete elements like footings.

q: 2. A compression member is termed as column or strut if the ratio of its effective length to the least lateral dimension is more than ...........
explain: If the slenderness ratio (Le/d) is less than 3, the member is considered a pedestal rather than a column.

q: 3. All columns shall be designed for an eccentricity not less than ...........
explain: Even if a column is nominally axially loaded, a minimum eccentricity of 20 mm must be considered to account for construction tolerances.

q: 4. The shape of a column should be ...........
explain: Columns can be designed in any shape (square, rectangle, circle, L-shape, T-shape) depending on the architectural and structural needs.

q: 5. When the ratio of effective length of the column to its least lateral dimension does not exceed 12, it is termed as a ...........
explain: A column is classified as short if its slenderness ratio (Le/d) is 12 or less (Note: some older texts used 15, but 12 is the standard).

q: 6. While designing a reinforced concrete pole as a column, it is considered as ...........
options: fixed at one end and hinged at the other end
explain: R.C.C. poles are generally embedded deep in the ground, providing a fixed-end condition at the base and continuity at the top.

q: 7. The purpose of lateral ties in short reinforced concrete columns is to ...........
options: increase the load carrying capacity of the column
explain: Lateral ties provide lateral support to the longitudinal bars to prevent them from buckling outward under high axial loads.

q: 8. A long column is one whose ratio of effective length to its least lateral dimension exceeds ...........
explain: If the ratio of effective length to least lateral dimension (Le/d) exceeds 12, it is classified as a long (slender) column.

q: 9. In a column, with helical reinforcement, the permissible load is based on the core area. The least lateral dimension of such a column should be taken as ...........
options: equal to the diameter of core
explain: In a helically reinforced column, the 'core' is the concrete area enclosed within the center-line of the helical reinforcement, and its diameter defines the least lateral dimension for specific calculations.

q: 10. The diameter of the polygonal links or lateral ties should not be less than....... of the diameter of the largest longitudinal bar ...........
explain: To provide adequate lateral restraint, the tie diameter must be at least one-fourth (1/4) the diameter of the largest longitudinal bar.

q: 11. A compression member is considered as short when both the slenderness ratio lex/D and ley/b are less than ...........
explain: A column is classified as short if the ratio of effective length to the corresponding lateral dimension is less than 12.

q: 12. The effective length of column with one and effectively held in position and other restrained against rotation at both directions is ...........
explain: For a column with both ends fixed against rotation and position, the theoretical value is 0.5l, but the design (recommended) value is 0.65l.

q: 13. The effective length of a column with both ends effectively held in position, but not restrained against rotation is ...........
explain: For a column with both ends hinged (held in position but free to rotate), the effective length is equal to the unsupported length 'l'.

q: 14. The maximum percentage of longitudinal reinforcement in R.C.C. columns is ...........
explain: Though 4% is common in practice to allow for lapping, the maximum theoretical limit is 6.0% of the gross cross-sectional area.

q: 15. The minimum diameter of longitudinal reinforcement in R.C.C. column should not be less than ...........
explain: Main longitudinal bars in a column must have a minimum diameter of 12 mm to ensure sufficient stiffness for the cage.

q: 16. The effective length of column is taken as ...........
options: the distance between the ends of column
twice the length between ends of column
the half length between the ends of column
the distance between the points of contra flexure
explain: The effective length (Le) is the distance between adjacent points of zero moment (points of contraflexure) in the buckling shape.

q: 17. The ratio of minimum area of cross section of longitudinal bars and gross sectional area of column shall be ...........
explain: Since the minimum percentage is 0.8%, this corresponds to 0.8/100, which simplifies to 1/125.

q: 18. The ratio of minimum number of longitudinal bars provided in rectangular columns to those in circular column is ...........
explain: Rectangular columns require a minimum of 4 bars (one in each corner), while circular columns require a minimum of 6 bars. The ratio is 4/6, which simplifies to 2/3.

q: 19. Spacing of longitudinal bars measured along the peripheral of the column should not exceed ...........
explain: As per IS 456, the maximum spacing between longitudinal bars along the periphery of the column is limited to 300 mm to prevent local buckling of the concrete face.

q: 20. A pedestal is said to be a compression member when its effective length does not exceed ...........
options: two times the least lateral dimension
three times the least lateral dimension
four times the least lateral dimension
explain: A vertical compression member is classified as a pedestal if its effective length is less than or equal to 3 times its least lateral dimension.

q: 21. The internal angle of laterals ties in the form of polygonal links in columns shall not exceed ...........
explain: To ensure effective lateral restraint and prevent the tie from 'opening' under pressure, the internal angle of a polygonal link should not exceed 135°.

q: 22. The minimum number of longitudinal steel bars in R.C.C. circular columns must be ...........
explain: For circular columns, 6 bars are required to properly maintain the circular shape of the reinforcement cage and provide uniform confinement.

q: 23. The minimum number of longitudinal steel bars in helically reinforced R.C.C. columns must be ...........
explain: Helical reinforcement is typically used in circular columns, which requires a minimum of 6 longitudinal bars for stability of the helix.

q: 24. The spacing of the longitudinal bars effectively tied should not exceed the following if additional longitudinal bars provided in between are tied in one direction by open ties ...........
explain: Specific detailing requirements for secondary ties/links often relate spacing to the diameter of the transverse reinforcement (48 times the tie diameter).

q: 25. The diameter of transverse reinforcement of columns should be equal to one fourth of the diameter of the main rods but not less than ...........
explain: While 5mm was the older standard, current practice (and many code versions) specifies a 6 mm minimum for transverse ties to ensure cage rigidity.

q: 26. The spacing of transverse reinforcement of a column shall not be more than ...........
options: the least lateral dimension of a column
sixteen times the smallest diameter of the longitudinal reinforcement bar to be tied
forty-eight times the diameter of the transverse reinforcement
explain: IS 456 pitch requirements for ties: Spacing should be the least of: 1) Least lateral dimension, 2) 16x smallest longitudinal bar diameter, or 3) 48x tie diameter.

q: 27. An additional longitudinal reinforcement in webs of beams should be placed if the depth of the web is more than 750 mm at
explain: Side face reinforcement is required in deep beams (web > 750mm) to control cracking due to shrinkage and temperature.

q: 28. The minimum lap length at the splice of compression reinforcement in a R.C.C member should be more than
options: 30 times the diameter of the bar
twice the development length or 30 times the diameter of the bar
48 times the diameter of the bar
24 times the diameter of the bar or development length
explain: In compression, the lap length is equal to the development length in compression but not less than 24φ.

q: 29. The ratio of the allowable ultimate crushing stress of R.C.C. columns in bending to that of 150 mm cube strength is
explain: Columns are subjected to axial compression; older codes used 0.85fck for column sections.

q: 30. The ratio of the ultimate load capacity of helically-reinforced concrete slender columns to that of tied columns is
explain: Helical reinforcement provides better lateral confinement to the concrete core compared to lateral ties, allowing for a 5% increase in load-carrying capacity according to standard codes.

q: 31. According to I.S.: 456-2000, in the case of slender columns, the permissible stresses in steel and concrete are reduced by multiplying with a coefficient Cr given by
explain: The reduction factor Cr accounts for the buckling tendency of slender columns. The standard formula relates the effective length (le) to the least radius of gyration (rmin).

q: 32. The precast concrete piles are generally used for a maximum design load of about...... except for large prestressed piles
explain: Standard precast RC piles are typically designed for loads up to 80 tonnes. For higher loads, prestressed piles or cast-in-situ piles are preferred.

q: 33. On designing reinforced concrete piles as a column, it is considered as
options: fixed at one end and hinged at the other end
explain: A pile is usually considered fixed at the bottom (embedded in hard strata) and hinged at the top (connection with the pile cap) for effective length calculations.

q: 34. According to load factor method, the permissible load W on a short column reinforced with longitudinal bars and lateral stirrups, is
options: stress in concrete x area of concrete
stress in steel x area of steel
stress in concrete x area of concrete + stress in steel x area of steel
explain: The load factor (Ultimate Strength) method calculates capacity by summing the ultimate strengths contributed by both the concrete and the longitudinal steel.

q: 35. If the size of column is reduced above the floor, the main bars of the columns, are
options: bent inward at the floor level
stopped just below the floor level and separate lap bars provided
explain: Depending on the degree of offset, bars can be cranked (bent) or terminated with new starter bars provided to maintain continuity.

q: 36. If the diameter of longitudinal bars of a square column is 16 mm, the diameter of lateral ties should not be less than
explain: Lateral ties must be at least 1/4th the diameter of the largest longitudinal bar (16/4 = 4mm) but not less than 5mm (or 6mm in modern codes).

q: 37. A pre-cast pile generally used, is
explain: Square piles with chamfered corners are preferred because they are easy to cast and the chamfering prevents damage to the corners during driving.

q: 38. The minimum number of main steel bars provided is R.C.C.
explain: Building codes specify minimum bars for geometry: 4 for rectangular, 6 for circular (to maintain the shape), and usually one per corner for polygons.
